title: House Paints and More vs. Precision Paint Experts
description: Comparing House Paints and More with Precision Paint Experts for a garage floor? Questions to ask about epoxy, polyaspartic coatings, and concrete prep.
h1: House Paints and More vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: A garage floor coating is only as strong as the concrete prep underneath. This guide helps North Central Florida homeowners compare floor coating bids.

secondary: garage floor epoxy north central florida
questions: What is the difference between epoxy and polyaspartic garage floor coatings?
Why does garage floor epoxy peel?

body: House Paints and More is one of the painting and property-service companies homeowners in North Central Florida may be comparing. If the project on your list is a garage floor, the comparison works differently from a wall repaint. A floor coating takes hot tires, dropped tools, chemical drips, and moisture pushing up from the slab below. The coating system and the prep behind it decide whether the floor still looks good in a few years or starts lifting in patches.
This guide does not comment on any other company's work. It explains the main coating types, lists questions to ask every bidder, and describes what Precision Paint Experts offers.

sections.h2: Epoxy and polyaspartic, in plain terms
body: Epoxy is a two-part coating that bonds to properly prepared concrete and builds a thick, durable layer. Polyaspartic coatings are a related family that cure faster and are often used as a topcoat or as a full system. Both can work well; the right choice depends on the slab, how the garage is used, and how quickly you need it back in service.
We install both garage floor epoxy and polyaspartic coatings. Our garage floor epoxy coating page explains the systems, and our epoxy garage floor installers page covers installation in more detail.

Most peeling floors trace back to one of a few causes: the concrete was not cleaned or profiled enough for the coating to bond, moisture was coming up through the slab, or a product meant for light use was put down in a working garage. Our article on why garage epoxy peels and how to fix it walks through each one. The takeaway for comparing bids is simple: ask how the slab will be prepared and whether moisture will be checked.
A lower bid that skips or shortens surface preparation is not really cheaper if the floor has to be ground off and recoated later. Prep is the line to read first.

sections.h2: Questions for any floor coating bid
body: Take this list to each estimate appointment:
bullets: Which coating system, by product name, and how many coats or layers?
How will the concrete be cleaned and prepared before coating?
Will the slab be checked for moisture first?
How are existing cracks or old coatings handled?
How long before I can walk on it, and before I can park on it?

body: A crew lead walks the garage, measures, photographs conditions, and takes moisture readings where needed. The written estimate names the coating products, lists prep steps and any excluded areas, and gives a schedule. Nothing is added later without your written approval, and the estimate usually arrives within one business day of the walkthrough.

If the walls, doors, or trim in the garage also need attention, they can be included on the same estimate. Ask for a quote through our free quote page, then line it up against any other bid, question by question.

faqs.q: Do you install polyaspartic as well as epoxy?
faqs.a: Yes. We install garage floor epoxy and polyaspartic coatings, and the system recommended for your slab is named on the estimate.

faqs.q: Will you check my slab for moisture?
faqs.a: Moisture readings are taken where needed during the walkthrough, before any coating is specified.

faqs.q: Is House Paints and More connected to Precision Paint Experts?
faqs.a: No. We are a separate, locally owned company. This page is a guide to comparing floor coating bids.
